content: Lindane is a medication used to treat lice and scabies, but it carries significant risks of severe side effects, including seizures and death. Safer alternatives are available, and Lindane should only be used if other treatments are not an option or have failed. Patients who experience severe side effects often misuse Lindane by applying too much, using it too frequently, or leaving it on for too long. However, even when used as directed, some individuals have experienced serious adverse effects. Certain populations are at higher risk for dangerous side effects, including infants, children, older adults, individuals weighing less than 110 pounds, and those with skin conditions such as psoriasis, rashes, scabby or broken skin. These individuals should only use Lindane if deemed absolutely necessary by a physician. Lindane must not be used in premature infants or individuals with a history of seizures, particularly if the seizures are difficult to control. Lindane is toxic if overused or applied for extended periods. Your doctor will provide specific instructions on how to use it safely. Follow these directions exactly. Do not use more Lindane than prescribed, do not leave it on longer than instructed, and do not repeat the treatment, even if symptoms persist. Itching may continue for several weeks after the lice or scabies have been eradicated. Lindane is available as a lotion for scabies and a shampoo for lice. It should only be used once and not reapplied for a long time. The lotion is for scabies treatment only and should not be used for lice. The shampoo is for head lice or pubic lice and should not be used for scabies. Always follow the instructions provided by your doctor or pharmacist and read the patient information leaflet carefully. When applying Lindane, ensure it is only used on the skin or hair. Avoid contact with the mouth, eyes, or any mucous membranes. Wear gloves made of nitrile, sheer vinyl, or latex with neoprene when applying Lindane to yourself or someone else. Do not use natural latex gloves, as they do not provide adequate protection. Dispose of the gloves after use and wash your hands thoroughly. After treatment, sanitize all clothing, bedding, and towels by washing them in very hot water or dry-cleaning them. For Lindane lotion, apply a thin layer to clean, dry skin from the neck down to the toes, including the soles of the feet. Do not use the lotion on the face or scalp. Leave the lotion on for 8–12 hours, but no longer, as prolonged exposure increases the risk of seizures and other serious problems. After this time, wash off the lotion with warm water (not hot water). Do not allow others to touch your skin while the lotion is on, as it can harm them. For Lindane shampoo, wash your hair with regular shampoo at least one hour before application and dry it thoroughly. Do not use any creams, oils, or conditioners. Shake the Lindane shampoo well and apply just enough to wet the hair, scalp, and small hairs on the back of the neck. If treating pubic lice, apply the shampoo to the pubic hair and underlying skin. Leave the shampoo on for exactly 4 minutes, keeping your hair uncovered during this time. After 4 minutes, lather the shampoo with a small amount of warm water and rinse it off completely. Dry your hair with a clean towel and use a fine-tooth comb or tweezers to remove lice eggs (nits) and larvae. Lindane should not be shared with others, as it may harm them. If you have scabies or pubic lice, inform your doctor if you have a sexual partner, as they may also need treatment to prevent reinfection. For head lice, all household members or close contacts may require treatment. Before using Lindane, inform your doctor if you are allergic to it or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, and supplements you are taking, as some drugs may interact with Lindane. Mention any history of seizures, head injuries, brain or spinal tumors, liver disease, or conditions such as HIV/AIDS. If you consume alcohol or have recently stopped drinking large amounts of alcohol, or if you have recently stopped using sedatives, inform your doctor. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should take special precautions, such as wearing gloves when applying Lindane to another person and discarding breast milk for 24 hours after use. Store Lindane in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from heat and moisture. Dispose of any unused or expired medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance. In case of overdose, contact a poison control center immediately at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or stops breathing, call 911. If Lindane is accidentally ingested, seek emergency help right away. If it gets into the eyes, rinse them with water immediately and seek medical attention if irritation persists. Keep all appointments with your doctor and do not let anyone else use your medication. Lindane prescriptions are not refillable, so consult your doctor if additional treatment is needed.
